questions.question: [NEET 2022 | Biology] Which have an open circulatory system?
questions.solution: ## **Correct Answer: (D) Cockroach and prawn** --- ## **Step-by-Step Reasoning:** ### **Circulatory Systems Overview:** | Organism | Circulatory Type | Details | |----------|------------------|---------| | **Earthworm** | **Closed** | Blood confined in vessels; contracts aortic arches pump blood | | **Cockroach** | **Open** | Blood (hemolymph) bathes organs directly in body cavity | | **Prawn** | **Open** | Blood (hemolymph) circulates through hemocoel | --- ## **Why Each Option is Correct/Incorrect:** | Option | Analysis | |--------|----------| | **(A) Earthworm** | \u₂₇₄c WRONG - Earthworms have a **closed** circulatory system | | **(B) Cockroach only** | \u₂₇₄c WRONG - Incomplete answer; prawn also has open circulation | | **(C) Prawn only** | \u₂₇₄c WRONG - Incomplete answer; cockroach also has open circulation | | **(D) Cockroach and prawn** | \u₂₇₀₅ **CORRECT** - Both are arthropods with open circulation | --- ## **Key Concept to Remember:** **ARTHROPODS = OPEN CIRCULATORY SYSTEM** - Cockroach, Prawn, Insects, Spiders, all arthropods have **hemocoel** (body cavity) - Blood flows freely around organs - Less efficient but requires lower metabolic rate **ANNELIDS = CLOSED CIRCULATORY SYSTEM** - Earthworms have true blood vessels - Blood contained in closed loops - More efficient oxygen transport --- ## **Quick Memory Tip:** \U₀₀₀₁f₅₃₄ **"Arthropods are OPEN house parties"** - their blood flows freely everywhere!

questions.question: [NEET 2019 | Biology] Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Chordata?
questions.solution: # Answer: **(D) Ventral heart** ## Why This Is The Answer The **three PRIMARY diagnostic characteristics of Chordata** are: 1. **Notochord** (A) \u₂₇₁₃₂. **Dorsal hollow nerve cord** (B) \u₂₇₁₃₃. **Pharyngeal gill slits** (C) \u₂₇₁₃ While it's TRUE that chordates have a **ventral heart**, this is NOT typically listed as one of the defining characteristics of the phylum Chordata in standard NCERT biology. --- ## Key Concept to Remember **The Three Defining Features of Chordata** (appear at some stage in all chordates): | Feature | Description | |---------|-------------| | **Notochord** | Flexible rod providing body support (replaced by vertebral column in vertebrates) | | **Dorsal Hollow Nerve Cord** | Nerve cord on the DORSAL (back) side, hollow throughout | | **Pharyngeal Gill Slits** | Present in pharynx at some developmental stage | --- ## Why Other Options Are Wrong - **(A) Notochord** - This is THE defining feature of all chordates - **(B) Dorsal hollow nerve cord** - Universal chordate feature - **(C) Pharyngeal gill slits** - Universal feature (even humans have pharyngeal pouches as embryos) - **(D) Ventral heart** - While TRUE in chordates, it's NOT a primary diagnostic criterion --- ## Exam Tip \U₀₀₀₁f₄a₁ Remember: When NEET asks about chordate characteristics, focus on the **"Big 3"** - Notochord, Dorsal Nerve Cord, and Pharyngeal Gill Slits. These are non-negotiable!

questions.question: The radial symmetry is observed in I.Platyhelminthes II.Coelenterates III.Aschelminthes IV.Annelids V.Echinoderms
